runningBalanceAfter.description: Computed running balance of glAccount for this loan account immediately after this line posts — callers never need a separate read to confirm the posting effect.

sourceEventId.description: Populated from the caller's Idempotency-Key header value. Every JournalEntry is keyed on this — never reused across two logically different postings.

postingRuleVersion.description: The exact version of the posting-rule manifest (specs/coa's sibling posting-rule catalog, docs/design-notes.md Appendix B) that produced this entry — so any entry can be explained after the fact even if the rule's logic later changes. Never inferred or backfilled; always the version in effect at posting time.

lines.description: Server-derived; sum of DEBIT line amounts always equals sum of CREDIT line amounts, per currency.

immutable.description: There is no update or delete operation for this resource. Corrections are always a new, separate entry with a new sourceEventId.

periodId.description: Calendar-month accounting period this entry belongs to, derived from postedAt (YYYY-MM). Once this period is closed, no entry belonging to it may be the target of a reversal — see reversalOfSourceEventId and POST /periods/{periodId}:close.

isPriorPeriodAdjustment.description: True only for a correction entry posted after adjustmentForPeriodId's period was closed. A prior-period adjustment always belongs to the CURRENT open period (periodId reflects when it was posted, not the period it corrects) — this flag plus adjustmentForPeriodId is what preserves the audit trail back to the closed period it corrects.

adjustmentForPeriodId.description: Set only when isPriorPeriodAdjustment is true — the closed period this entry corrects. Null otherwise.

metadata.description: Rule-specific audit context. See GLPostingAPI's PostingRuleCode catalog for which rules require it and what it must carry.

JournalEntry.description: Income-recognition principle governing every posting rule in this catalog: income accounts (InterestIncome, FeeIncome) are credited exactly once, at accrual or assessment time (PR-ACCR-01, PR-DELINQ-01). Every subsequent cash-collection entry (PR-REPAY-01, PR-PAYOFF-01) clears Cash against the corresponding Receivable account (InterestReceivable, FeeReceivable, LoanReceivable) — it never re-credits Income. The one legitimate exception is a waiver (PR-DELINQ-02), which reverses Income directly because it undoes the original recognition rather than collecting against it.
